title: Sass Review Quiz
description: Review the small examples from this Sass course. Take your time and read the reason given for each answer.

questions.question: Which file does the browser read after Sass builds your styles?
questions.explanation: Sass is a tool that turns a style recipe into CSS. The browser reads the CSS file, so it does not need to understand the Sass recipe.

questions.question: What starts a Sass variable name?
questions.explanation: A Sass variable gives a value a name. The dollar sign starts that name. You can reuse one colour without typing its code each time.

questions.question: Which heading does the nested h2 rule choose?
questions.explanation: Nesting puts a rule inside another rule. Sass joins the selectors. This can show that a small part belongs inside a bigger part.

questions.question: What does & stand for in this nested rule?
questions.explanation: The ampersand sign stands for the selector around it. It is useful when the same element changes state, such as a button being focused.

questions.question: Which command uses a mixin?
questions.explanation: A mixin is a named group of CSS choices. Include it wherever you want those choices copied into a rule.

questions.question: Which colour does frame use when no input is given?
questions.explanation: A mixin can take an input value. A default value is used when the caller does not provide one.

questions.question: How do you read ink from the colours module?
questions.explanation: A module is a Sass file that shares values or recipes. @use loads it and gives its members a clear name prefix.

questions.question: What is math.div(24px, 2)?
questions.explanation: The Sass math module has tools for calculations. math.div divides values while Sass builds the stylesheet.

questions.question: Which value is stored under the key sun?
questions.explanation: A map pairs names with values, like labels on paint pots. map.get looks up the value for one label.

questions.question: How much margin does space-3 get?
questions.explanation: An @each loop makes one rule for each item in a list. It saves repeated typing when the rule shape stays the same.

questions.question: What does this function return?
questions.explanation: A Sass function calculates one value and returns it. A mixin writes a group of declarations instead.

questions.question: When does this card use 2rem padding?
options: Only when the card contains two paragraphs
When the viewport is at least 40rem wide
questions.explanation: Sass can group a screen-size rule with the component it styles. The output is still a normal CSS media query.
